title: Comparison and equality
learningObjectives: Explain comparison and equality and write clear, safe expressions.

understand.concept: Comparison operators compare values using relational operators such as <, >, <=, and >=, and equality operators == and ===. Strict equality avoids type coercion, while loose equality applies coercion rules. Object equality compares identity, not object contents.
understand.whyItMatters: Choosing strict equality by default avoids many surprising conversions. Comparisons can also produce false for values that seem similar when types differ.
understand.analogy: Comparison asks whether two values meet a relationship; strict equality checks both value and type without coercion.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; operator evaluation and coercion follow JavaScript precedence and conversion rules.

explain.narrative: Strict equality is false for a number and string; loose equality converts them and returns true. The relational comparison returns true.

examples.explanation: Strict equality is false for a number and string; loose equality converts them and returns true. The relational comparison returns true.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page displays the expression results described.

practise.guidedTask: Compare values using == and ===. Predict the results for numbers, strings, null, and undefined before running the code.
practise.independentTask: Write a small program that uses the operator or numeric rule in a practical example. Predict results, run the code, and explain any coercion.
hints: Preserve valid falsy values when using defaults.
Validate numeric inputs and check finite results.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Comparison and equality</title></head><body>
<script>console.log(5==='5');console.log(5=='5');console.log(8>=6);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Which equality operator compares without type coercion?
questions.explanation: Strict equality does not perform type coercion.

questions.prompt: What should you do before using a value in a numeric calculation?
options: Assume it is already a valid number
questions.explanation: Explicit conversion and validation prevent invalid or imprecise values from entering calculations.
